829. Since religion resides in the highest parts of a human being, and his lower parts live and shine from these highest parts, and because Mohammed resides in their minds along with their religion, some Mohammed is always placed in their sight. And so that they may turn their faces toward the East, upon which the Lord is, he is placed below the Christian center. It is not the Mohammed himself who wrote the <term>Alcoran</term> <gloss>Koran</gloss>, but another who performs his duty; nor is it always the same one, but he is changed. Once it was a man from Saxony, who, having been captured by the Algerians, became a Mohammedan. Because he had also been a Christian, he was sometimes moved to speak with them about the Lord, saying that He was not the Son of Joseph, but the Son of God Himself. Later, others succeeded this Mohammed. In the place where that representative Mohammed has his seat, a fire appears like a torch so that he may be recognized; but that fire is visible to no one except the Mohammedans.

830. The Mohammed himself who wrote the <term>Alcoran</term> <gloss>Koran</gloss> does not come into sight today. I was told that in the earliest times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over all things of their religion as God, he was cast out from his seat, which he had under the Catholics, and was sent down to the right side near the south. Once, a certain society of Mohammedans was stirred up by malicious people to acknowledge Mohammed as God. In order that the sedition might be quelled, Mohammed was brought up from the lower earth and shown, and then he was also seen by me. He appeared similar to corporeal spirits, who have no interior perception, with a face tending toward black. I heard him speaking these words: *I am your Mohammed*; and immediately he seemed to sink down.

831. The Mohammedans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the faith in three Divine Persons, and consequently the worship of three Gods and just as many Creators. Furthermore, they are hostile to the Roman Catholics because of their genuflections before images, and therefore they call the latter idolaters and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, and that they speak of one while muttering three, and consequently that they divide Omnipotence and make three out of one and the One. And they say that they are like Fauns with three horns, one for every god and three together for one, and that they pray thus, sing psalms thus, and sound off from the pulpits thus.

832. The Mohammedans, like all nations that acknowledge one God and love what is just and do what is good out of religion, have their own Heaven, but it is outside the Christian one. The Mohammedan Heaven is divided into two. In the Lower [Heaven] they live honestly with many wives, but from there no others are raised into the higher Heaven except those who renounce concubines and acknowledge the Lord our Savior, and at the same time His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but that it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This faith among them is the means by which ascent into the higher Heaven is granted to them by the Lord.

833. That the Mohammedan religion has been received by more kingdoms than the Christian religion can be a scandal to those who think about Divine Providence and at the same time believe that no one can be saved except one who is born a Christian. But the Mohammedan religion is not a scandal to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence; these inquire in what it consists and also find it. It consists in this: that the Mohammedan religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the Wisest of all, and also as the Son of God. But because they have made only the <term>Alcoran</term> <gloss>Koran</gloss> the book of their religion, and therefore Mohammed, who wrote it, has settled into their thoughts and they follow him with some worship, they therefore think little about our Lord. So that it may be fully known that that religion was raised up by the Divine Providence of the Lord for the sake of destroying the idolatries of many nations, it will be told in some order, but first concerning the origin of idolatries.
